newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai trust fund due for launch in Feb 1997.
newsitem.headline: Thai trust fund due for launch in Feb 1997.

text.p: The Stock Exchange of Thailand (SET) said on Monday it expects to launch next February the Thai trust fund, a vehicle designed to help foreign investors circumvent Thai corporate ownership limits.
SET president Singh Tangtatswas told reporters the bourse and the Securities and Exchange Commission had completed the legal process for getting the fund started.

SET officials said the Thai market's extended bear move this year would, ironically, help the launch of the fund as the slump has narrowed premiums that Thai blue-chip stocks fetch on the bourse's foreign board over prices quoted on its main board.
"I think it is the right time (to lauch the funds) because the premium (prices) are not that much different from the main board," SET vice president Suvicha Mingkwan said.
The composite SET Index closed at its 51-month low of 819.79 on Monday on Thailand's weak economic outlook and concern about quality of property loans extended by commercial banks.

Foreign investors can buy units in the Thai incorporated mutual fund which, in turn, will purchase on their behalf shares of Thai firms above current 25-49 percent foreign ownership limits set by these firms.

SET senior vice president Patareeya Benjapolchai said about 40 to 50 listed firms had earlier this year expressed interest in setting aside, through the trust fund, some of their outstanding shares for foreign investors.

Another SET official said he expects 20-30 Thai firms will initially make shares available through the fund but he said many major Thai banks, especially those whose shares fetch high premiums on the foreign board, have not applied to participate in the new investment vehicle for foreigners.
He said these banks are cocerned that its launch would hurt prices of their stocks on both main and foreign boards.
Bangkok Bank Plc and Thai Farmers Bank Plc closed on the foreign board on Monday at 262 baht and 158 baht against, respectively, 194 and 125 on the main board.
